prompt: A printable US Letter portrait page (8.5 by 11 inches) for a kids' pretend-play game, drawn flat and straight-on and filling the whole image: the page itself, not a photo or mockup of paper. Plain white paper with a clean white margin of about half an inch on every side where nothing is drawn, so it prints on a home printer. The game is "Pirate Treasure Hunt". Art style for the whole kit: coloring-page version of a friendly flat vector cartoon: black outlines only on white paper, thick clean even lines, soft rounded shapes, no color, no gray, no shading, no filled black areas, every shape open for a 5-year-old to color in. Letters are bold outlined bubble letters that can be colored in too. Draw a sheet of exactly 4 lanyard name badges, laid out 2 columns and 2 rows, all the same size: tall rounded-rectangle tags with a punched hole and a little clip at the top center, a themed decorative border, one character picture in the upper half, the role title under it on a ribbon banner, and at the bottom the word "Name:" followed by a long blank line to write on. In order: badge 1: a cute cartoon character as the captain (pirate hat and a treasure chest key), title "Captain"; badge 2: a cute cartoon character as the map reader (holding a rolled map), title "Map Reader"; badge 3: a cute cartoon character as the clue finder (holding a magnifying glass), title "Clue Finder"; badge 4: a cute cartoon character as the lookout (holding a spyglass, parrot on shoulder), title "Lookout". The ONLY words on the page, spelled exactly letter for letter: "Captain", "Map Reader", "Clue Finder", "Lookout", "Name:". "Name:" appears once on every badge (4 times). Big, clear, rounded print letters, easy for a 5-year-old to read, dark on a light background, never curved along a path, never tiny. No other words, letters, numbers or signatures anywhere. Every badge identical in shape and size so they look like a set. Thin gray dashed cut lines around each piece, with wide white gutters between pieces so scissors fit. Kid-friendly and gentle, for ages 4 to 8: no guns, no knives, no real weapons (a toy sword is fine), no blood, nothing scary, no real people, no brands, no logos.
